The 1973 winner, Marjorie Wallace, was stripped of her title on 8 March 1974 because she had failed to fulfill the basic requirements of the job. Miss World's organizers did not elect someone to serve in her place. In 1976, several countries boycotted the pageant because it included both a white and a black contestant from South Africa.

A number of contestants followed the lead of Kathrine Sørland of Norway in boycotting the contest (despite the controversy, Sørland became a semi-finalist in both the Miss World and Miss Universe contests), while others, such as Costa Rica, were instructed by their national governments and parliaments not to attend. Among the other boycotting nations were Denmark, Spain, Switzerland, Panama, Belgium and Kenya. Lawal asked that contestants not suspend their participation in the contest, saying that it was for the good of her country and that they could, as the representative of Sweden had earlier remarked, make a much stronger case for her on the ground in Nigeria.
The Miss World Organization later allowed her to compete at Miss World 2016. After the 2019 pageant, the organization chose Thailand as the host country of Miss World 2020, to be held in Phuket.

Miss World was originally scheduled to be held in the United Arab Emirates. The pageant was later moved to India, and set to be held on 16 December 2023 in Delhi. It was later postponed to 2 March 2024 due to the 2023 elections in India, and later postponed once again to 9 March 2024 in Mumbai.

Miss World began in New Delhi in February 2024 with its pre-pageant challenges, with Pyszková going on to place as a top four finalist for Europe in the top model challenge and as a top 10 finalist in the Beauty with a Purpose Challenge.

The Miss World pageant is the longest running major international pageant. Miss World was created in 1951 by Eric Morley in the United Kingdom. web.description: Opal Suchata makes history as the first Thai Miss World 2025, inspiring millions with her advocacy, resilience, and global vision.
snippets: She was crowned by the outgoing Miss World, Krystyna Pyszkova, and shared the honor with other top finalists from Ethiopia, Poland, and Martinique, who also received continental queen titles. Opal's education is also as commendable as her pageantry victory. Born on March 20, 2003, in Phuket, Thailand, she grew up in a hospitality business family.

Opal intends to sponsor a number of charitable causes, specifically in women's health, and to be an inspiration to others all around the world through her composure and determination. Her journey from being a young breast cancer survivor to becoming an international beauty queen and advocate represents the way that overcoming adversity can become the genesis of powerful leadership and global citizenship. The grand coronation took place in Telangana, India, where she won over 107 international delegates in a dazzling ceremony. Her victory marks a significant milestone for Thailand, which had waited over 72 years for a Miss World crown.

Prior to winning the title of Miss World 2025, she was Thailand's representative at Miss Universe 2024 and took home the third runner-up title. Her Miss Universe crown was subsequently forfeited due to contract breach.
